text:
Pause on the section's explanatory diagram
for a complete evidence

reading of Iteration 21 — NAS-Bench-201
within-slice confirmation. First,

identify the research question before
looking at the answer. The

question asks whether the fixed components
create a meaningful ordering

surface, whether a particular neighborhood
provides useful guidance on that

surface, or whether a cheaper executor is
equally effective. The

sample is 40 seeds, and the source
artifact is production

brief and paper source. The horizontal
axis names the recorded

independent quantity—such as permutation
size, position, distance, or

distinct evaluations. The vertical axis
names the measured outcome—such as

accuracy, error, hit probability, regret,
correlation, or hitting time. Raw

points remain visible when their count
permits. A summary line

or bar describes those points; it does not
replace them.

A capped observation receives a censor
marker, and a sampled

landscape never pretends to be
exhaustively enumerated. The central

supports this finding: Use
operation-multiset slices with at least 60

placements and at least a one-point
accuracy range. The correct

limitation is: The conclusion is scoped to
the recorded evaluator,

landscape, and budget. That limitation
rules out a broader promotional

interpretation while preserving the result
actually measured. The decision

carried into the research program is:
Carry this constraint into

the next experiment and compare methods at
equal cost. Finally,

compare against the equal-budget
alternative. Generations, repeated cache

hits, and distinct evaluations are not
interchangeable. A method earns

a search-efficiency claim only when
uncertainty, evaluator resolution,

optimum density, and evaluation cost have
all been accounted for.
